plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (three-cavity Fabry-Perot dual-band filter) based on iteration_14 results (best_target_score=0.911). Four routes explore: (1) L-BFGS-B optimizer with QWOT-seeded initialization per feedback directive, (2) reduced 19-layer topology to test layer count efficiency, (3) alternative IR material pair (Si/ZnS) to assess material sensitivity, (4) modified cavity coupling with explicit spacer layer control. All routes maintain 21-layer or specified fixed topology, Ge/ZnS or alternative dielectric pair, CaF2 substrate, normal incidence, and the four transmittance objectives across dual passbands (4.15-4.35 μm, 4.55-4.75 μm) and dual stopbands (3.60-4.00 μm, 4.85-5.20 μm).

routes.title: L-BFGS-B Optimized Three-Cavity Filter with QWOT-Seeded Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Curvature-aware L-BFGS-B optimization with Hessian approximation, initialized at ±20% jittered quarter-wave optical thickness estimates, will navigate flat-gradient regions near resonance peaks more effectively than gradient descent, yielding higher target scores and improved robustness margins for the three-cavity Ge/ZnS topology.
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with computational optimization using second-order information for step sizing in thickness space
routes.proposed_topology: 21-layer alternating Ge/ZnS stack on CaF2 substrate: Air|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|CaF2
manufacturing_considerations: thickness bounds 50-500 nm for deposition control
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for Fabry-Perot cavity formation
L-BFGS-B optimization with Hessian approximation for non-convex thickness spaces
expected_advantages: Better convergence in flat-gradient regions near resonance
Higher target scores than gradient descent baseline
known_risks: L-BFGS-B may converge to different local minima than gradient descent
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 21-layer alternating Ge/ZnS dielectric bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate for normal incidence. Layer sequence: Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge (21 finite layers). Initialize all layer thicknesses using quarter-wave optical thickness estimates at 4.45 μm center wavelength with ±20% uniform random jitter, bounded to 50-500 nm per layer. Optimize using L-BFGS-B algorithm with Hessian approximation enabled. Evaluate transmittance at four wavelength bands: maximize in 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm, minimize in 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Changed optimizer from gradient descent to L-BFGS-B with Hessian approximation and reinitialized thicknesses with ±20% QWOT jitter per feedback directive to explore adjacent harmonic basins with curvature-aware step sizing

routes.title: Reduced 19-Layer Three-Cavity Filter for Layer Count Efficiency
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 19-layer Ge/ZnS three-cavity topology can achieve comparable dual-band transmittance performance to the 21-layer design while reducing total film thickness and fabrication complexity, testing whether 21 layers exceeds the minimum required for this spectral specification.
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with reduced layer count to assess efficiency trade-offs
routes.proposed_topology: 19-layer alternating Ge/ZnS stack on CaF2 substrate: Air|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|CaF2
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot cavity theory relating layer count to bandwidth and transmittance
Trade-off between spectral performance and fabrication complexity
expected_advantages: Comparable performance if 21 layers is over-designed
known_risks: Reduced layer count may limit stopband rejection
May not achieve dual-band separation with only 19 layers

Initialize all layer thicknesses using quarter-wave optical thickness estimates at 4.45 μm center wavelength with ±20% uniform random jitter, bounded to 50-500 nm per layer. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. routes.revision_reason: Reduced layer count from 21 to 19 to test whether the 21-layer topology exceeds minimum requirements for dual-band specification, exploring efficiency trade-offs

routes.title: Alternative Material Pair: Si/ZnS Three-Cavity Filter
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Replacing Ge with Si as the high-index material while retaining ZnS as low-index will maintain comparable dual-band performance while potentially reducing absorption losses in the 4-5 μm range, testing material sensitivity of the three-cavity topology.
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with alternative high-index material to assess absorption and index contrast effects
routes.proposed_topology: 21-layer alternating Si/ZnS stack on CaF2 substrate: Air|Si|ZnS|Si|ZnS|Si|ZnS|Si|ZnS|Si|ZnS|Si|ZnS|Si|ZnS|Si|ZnS|Si|ZnS|Si|ZnS|Si|CaF2
manufacturing_considerations: Si and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
Si may have lower absorption than Ge in 4-5 μm range
theory_basis: High-low index material pair selection for mid-IR filters
Material absorption characteristics affecting peak transmittance
expected_advantages: Potentially lower absorption losses than Ge
Tests material sensitivity of optimized topology
Si may offer better thermal stability
known_risks: Si refractive index differs from Ge, requiring re-optimization
Si absorption in 4-5 μm range must be verified

routes.revision_reason: Changed high-index material from Ge to Si to test material sensitivity and potential absorption improvements while maintaining 21-layer three-cavity topology

routes.title: Modified Cavity Coupling with Explicit Spacer Control
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Explicitly controlling spacer layer thicknesses (layers 7-8, 14-15) to enforce cavity resonance conditions while optimizing mirror layers will improve dual-band separation by decoupling cavity tuning from mirror optimization, testing whether structured initialization improves convergence.
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with structured cavity spacing to enforce resonance conditions independently from mirror optimization
routes.proposed_topology: 21-layer alternating Ge/ZnS stack on CaF2 substrate: Air|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|CaF2
design_variables: all 21 layer thicknesses (50-500 nm bounds), with spacer layers 7-8 and 14-15 initialized at λ/2n estimates
manufacturing_considerations: spacer layers may require tighter thickness control
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot cavity resonance condition: spacer thickness determines passband center wavelength
Mirror layers control bandwidth and stopband rejection
expected_advantages: Improved dual-band separation through explicit cavity control
Faster convergence by decoupling cavity and mirror optimization
Better physical interpretability of optimized design
known_risks: Structured initialization may constrain search space too tightly
May not find global optimum if cavity-mirror coupling is important
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 21-layer alternating Ge/ZnS dielectric bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate for normal incidence. Layer sequence: Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge|ZnS|Ge (21 finite layers). Initialize mirror layers (1-6, 9-13, 16-21) using quarter-wave optical thickness estimates at 4.45 μm with ±20% jitter. Initialize spacer layers (7-8, 14-15) using half-wave optical thickness estimates at 4.45 μm with ±10% jitter to enforce cavity resonance. Bound all layers to 50-500 nm. Optimize using gradient descent algorithm. Evaluate transmittance at four wavelength bands: maximize in 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm, minimize in 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Added structured initialization separating spacer layers (cavity-defining) from mirror layers to test whether explicit cavity control improves dual-band separation convergence
